scenarios.title: Type, ability, and power/toughness layer dependency analogue

battlefield: one synthetic permanent with a printed keyword

actions: register later ability-removal and power/toughness effects
expectedOutcome: dependency ordering is honored inside the type layer
ability removal applies after type changes
base characteristics remain unchanged
power/toughness set and modify sublayers compose in order
scenarios.notes: A generic Blood Moon/Humility/Opalescence-class regression without depending on those exact cards. It verifies the reusable layer/dependency machinery those interactions require.

scenarios.title: Multiple noncommutative replacement effects require affected-player ordering
actions: register add-one and double life-gain replacements
affected player orders add-one before double
expectedOutcome: event pauses before mutation
chosen order is applied exactly once per replacement
one life becomes four life
rulesReferences: CR 616 — Interaction of Replacement and/or Prevention Effects
scenarios.notes: Locks in both the choice boundary and the replacement trace so future refactors cannot silently pick an engine-defined order.

scenarios.title: Simultaneous lethal damage produces one SBA batch and simultaneous death triggers
actions: deal lethal damage to both creatures in one damage batch
expectedOutcome: both damage events commit before state-based actions
both creatures die in the same SBA batch
both dies triggers are created before priority
scenarios.notes: Guards against sequential-death bugs where the first death changes whether the second event or trigger occurs.

scenarios.title: Four-player simultaneous triggers use rotated APNAP stack ordering

battlefield: one end-step trigger source per player

expectedOutcome: active player's trigger is stacked first
nonactive players follow turn order from the active player
the last stacked trigger belongs to the player immediately before the active player in turn order
rulesReferences: CR 603.3b — APNAP ordering of simultaneous triggers
scenarios.notes: Commander-specific stress case because four-player APNAP ordering differs from two-player intuition.

scenarios.title: Four-player elimination unwinds ownership, control, stack, choices, turns, and combat references atomically

battlefield: surviving-owned permanent stolen by doomed player

expectedOutcome: owned objects of eliminated player leave the game
surviving-owned stolen object returns to a surviving controller when possible
doomed player's stack/trigger/choice/turn/combat references are removed
turn order skips eliminated player
rulesReferences: CR 800.4a — player leaving a multiplayer game
scenarios.notes: High-risk transactional scenario: partial cleanup can corrupt multiplayer state in ways that surface many turns later.

scenarios.title: Control change invalidates a control-sensitive Aura and SBA removes it

battlefield: Aura enchanting a creature its controller controls

expectedOutcome: Aura relationship is re-evaluated using current control
illegal Aura is put into its owner's graveyard
host remains under new controller
scenarios.notes: Ensures control changes do not leave stale attachment legality cached in UI or state.

scenarios.title: Commander movement uses replacement timing for hand/library and SBA timing for graveyard/exile
actions: attempt commander move to hand and decline replacement
run state-based actions and choose command zone
expectedOutcome: hand/library command-zone choice occurs before the move
graveyard/exile command-zone choice occurs after the move
commander identity persists through both paths
scenarios.notes: Prevents conflating the two commander movement mechanisms into one replacement path.

scenarios.title: Copied permanent receives copiable base values, then later type and ability layers recalculate
expectedOutcome: copiable values remain 4/4 with printed copied ability
derived type change applies after copy layer
derived ability removal does not rewrite copiable values
scenarios.notes: Locks in the distinction between copiable values and current derived characteristics.

scenarios.title: Regression: resolving search spell remains authoritative while waiting for a library choice
actions: pass priority until resolution requests search choice
expectedOutcome: pendingResolution retains the physical spell while choice is open
invariants remain valid
choice resumes resolution
spell finishes in graveyard
scenarios.notes: Permanent regression for the Step 33 bug where a spell paused on a search choice could disappear from authoritative state or be overwritten by another resolving spell.
